slides.title: A home for decisions, evidence and progress
slides.body: Page 16. Title "A home for decisions, evidence and progress". Subtitle "The human sees what needs judgment and what the agents can continue". Inside app active Labeling. Left sidebar about 16% width with 'Definition', 'Guideline', active 'Rounds', 'Decision history'. Main central 54%: header "Decisions waiting for you" and pale teal small badge "3 open questions". Below three spacious rows with small document icons and status pills: "Can practical help count?" with 'Ready to review' and primary button 'Open report'; "When does tone change the label?" with 'Needs your judgment'; "What makes a case hard?" with 'More evidence requested'. Lower central quiet strip "Continue later. Your draft stays saved." Right 30% column header "Agent activity", small orange robot icon, card "Meaning Agent" / "Preparing contrasting learning cases", card "Expression Agent" / "Waiting for an approved guideline", then a teal document panel "Current standard" / "Guideline v1" / "Reviewed labels available". A modest optional-chat text link "Add context in chat" below. Do not show generic KPIs, model settings, or fabricated progress percentages. Clearly a calm decision inbox integrated in Rounds.
slides.notes: Proposed UI home inside the existing Labeling > Rounds surface, not a competing Workbench shell. Three questions and versions are synthetic design examples. The human sees pending decisions, saved drafts and separate agent states. Waiting for approval blocks dependent expression work only; the Meaning Agent can continue learning-case preparation. Definition, Guideline and history remain accessible; chat is supplementary. The page is a static illustration, not a functioning server implementation.

slides.title: One question, with the evidence beside it
slides.body: Page 17. Title "One question, with the evidence beside it". Subtitle "Choose a rule, add context, or leave the question open". App active Labeling. Breadcrumb "Rounds / Report 03 / Decision 01". Main content two columns: left 35% purple-tinted evidence panel headed "Why this question?" with current-rule snippet "Current rule: meaningful support" and two contrasting source cards "L01 · Practical help" / "I can help you rehearse." and "L02 · Reassurance" / "It makes sense to feel nervous." Below small source link "View source and context". Right 65% large decision form heading "Can practical help count as support?" and SIX separate radio options all empty and UNSELECTED: "A  Either kind can count"; "B  Reassurance is required"; "C  Use separate labels"; "None of these options"; "Write my own rule"; "Defer this decision". Beneath choices an empty text field labeled "Comments / my rule" with placeholder "Add a condition or explain your choice". Sticky bottom form bar buttons "Save draft" (outlined) and "Submit answers" (teal filled). Small helper line "Submit answered cards. Return to the rest later." A small neutral gray badge at form header 'No answer selected'. All six radio options clearly distinct. No auto-check or selected circle. No extra diagram arrows.
slides.notes: A rule-level form uses learning evidence and traceable human sources. All options start unselected. Rejection, custom proposal, deferral and unanswered are distinct stored states. Custom rules require text; conditional comments may require a clarified interpretation. Saving a draft is not approval. Explicitly submitting an exact displayed rule patch can approve only that shown scope; an abstract preference such as the displayed A/B/C choices needs integration into exact meaning before executable rule release when interpretation remains. Partial answers can be submitted. Nothing on this static mockup changes actual user preferences.

slides.title: The user can see what changed
slides.body: Page 18. Title "The user can see what changed". Subtitle "Submitted decisions become traceable rule changes and a review queue". App active Labeling. Header "Report 03 · Feedback received" with teal check and smaller status "Integration preview". Two equal panels side by side. Left teal panel "Guideline" with version line "v1 to proposed v2". Section "Your confirmed decision" / "Practical help can count." Below before/after blocks "Before" / "Meaningful support" then "Proposed wording" / "Relevant practical help or emotional reassurance can count." Yellow small flag below "Tone exception still needs clarification". Right purple/teal panel "Affected items" with tab labels active "Needs review" and inactive "Human-reviewed". Three spacious illustrative rows with IDs only and diagnostic tags: "L01" / "Practical help" / "Needs review"; "L03" / "Dismissive tone" / "Uncertain"; "L08" / "Boundary case" / "Hard". Below right panel two distinct status chips "Rule decision recorded" (teal) and "Item labels await review" (amber). Bottom left button "Review proposed wording" and bottom right text link "Open remaining question". Footer extra short sentence "Rule approval does not approve every affected label." No chart, no fake accuracy. The proposed new wording is visibly a proposal, not already released.
slides.notes: This screen makes scope and lineage visible after submission. A preference-only choice is recorded as a decision; the agent proposes executable wording and seeks clarification when necessary. An exact patch already approved on its report does not need a redundant confirmation. Here the wording is a proposal, not a released guideline. Affected labels remain a review queue and are not automatically human-approved. Diagnostics such as hard and uncertain are separate from task labels and require approved criteria. Atomic releases bind rules, compatible references and unresolved exclusions. All shown cases are synthetic.

slides.title: A separate space for expression experiments
slides.body: Page 19. Title "A separate space for expression experiments". Subtitle "The agent tests clearer wording while the approved meaning stays fixed". App active Quality. Left compact sidebar 'Evaluation' active, 'Final test', 'Audit'. Top main content a teal lock ribbon "Approved meaning v2" and blue badge "Expression candidate e03". Two columns. Left 55% a blue-outline panel headed "Compare executors" containing a clean FOUR-column table with headers 'Executor', 'Quality', 'Coverage', 'Speed' and exactly THREE rows: 'Small model', 'Mid-size model', 'Strong model'. All metric cells display an em dash placeholder, no numeric values. Status below table "Not run" and button "Review run settings". Beneath table readable small label "Validation summaries only". Right 45% orange-accent panel "Expression Agent" with small orange robot and three short checklist lines "Preserve every approved rule"; "Test learning cases"; "Compare validation summaries". Under that an amber escalation card "Meaning question?" / "Prepare an issue for the Meaning Agent" with button "View issue draft". Bottom thin shared strip "Human decisions stay in the Meaning Loop" with an arrow-like chevron from Expression Agent to Meaning Agent, NOT directly to a person. Footer "Illustrative setup. No model results yet." Do not show training knobs or tuning model weights.
slides.notes: Operator-facing Quality view. No measurements have been collected; dashes are intentionally unrun metrics, not missing favorable results. Runtime model slots do not prescribe actual providers or parameter counts. The Expression Agent calls fixed-weight executors, inspects learning errors, and uses bounded validation summaries for selection. It cannot access raw validation examples or rewrite the approved meaning. Quality and coverage floors and stronger-model non-regression constrain weak-model improvement; a narrow gap alone is insufficient. Semantic problems route to the Meaning Agent, which handles any human question. Independent final qualification occurs after selection, with frozen references hidden from executors.

slides.title: Large-scale labeling stays inspectable
slides.body: Page 20. Title "Large-scale labeling stays inspectable". Subtitle "The same delivery view serves both starting points". App active Delivery. Left compact sidebar active 'Scan', 'Review queue', 'Final labels', 'Handoff'. Main header "Batch labeling" with status pill "Awaiting qualification". A horizontal three-stage row across upper main content with purple document icon "New corpus items", blue chips "Qualified executor", purple checked documents "Labeled batches". Below two equal columns. LEFT panel header "Before starting" with three unchecked list entries "Freeze guideline and expression"; "Pass independent qualification"; "Set review and audit policy". Under this a clearly disabled gray button "Start batch" and label "Available after qualification". RIGHT panel header "Review and acceptance" with three colored queue labels "Uncertain items"; "Random audit sample"; "Open meaning questions". Below a document export panel "Delivery package" with lines "Structured guideline", "Labels with review status", "Unresolved cases and audit report". Bottom statement "Show which labels a person reviewed and which a batch policy accepted." No progress percentages, no completion checkmarks, no invented counts, no real dataset. Small footer page20.
slides.notes: Both the rough-idea and legacy-labeled entry points converge on this governed delivery workflow. This illustrative setup is awaiting qualification; the disabled Start batch control makes that dependency explicit. The production interface records batch/attempt lineage, resumes incomplete work, and separates uncertain-item review from population audit samples. Random audit includes low-risk items, and independent initial audit judgments precede revealing model predictions. Exported labels distinguish individually reviewed, inferred, accepted under audit policy and unresolved statuses. A frozen guideline travels with the labels and audit evidence. Real model/production Runs are not started by creating this mockup.
